messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired — PD-INC-8742 — gpu-pool-nyc-4: sustained CUDA OOMs (cudaMalloc failures). Severity: P1. Auto-notify to #eng-oncall and pagerduty. Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/pd/8742

samir: ack — I'm oncall, looking now.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD-INC-8742 acknowledged by samir. Escalation window paused.

danielle: seeing repeated traces on nyc-gpu-04..07: `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` interleaved with `kvcache eviction` spikes. Happens when context lengths > 2048 for model-rw-13. Paste of recent excerpt:

```
2026-02-18T10:02:11Z model-server[pid=4123]: ERROR allocate: cudaMalloc(&ptr, 134217728) -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-02-18T10:02:11Z model-server[pid=4123]: stack: tensor::alloc -> cuda::alloc -> nvml:memoryAlloc
2026-02-18T10:02:12Z kvcache[pid=2211]: INFO evicting 12 prefixes (total 45MB) due to pressure
```

ryan: probable traffic pattern: a few clients (chat-qa-prod) sent many long context requests simultaneously. Suggest: 1) temporarily drain pool from new allocations, 2) reroute chat-qa-prod to dedicated-2 or fallback-medium, 3) restart affected model servers to clear fragmentation.

danielle: starting step 1 — preventing new allocations on pool nyc-gpu-4: `redwoodctl pool update nyc-gpu-4 --allow-new=false` (applied).

infra-runner: kicking rolling restart on pods pinned to gpu-04: `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-server-nyc-gpu-04` — doing 1 pod at a time, maxUnavailable=1. I'll watch NVML metrics during restarts.

samir: applying aggressive kv-cache eviction policy for the pool as a short-term mitigation: `PATCH /internal/pools/nyc-gpu-4 { \"kvcache_eviction\": \"aggressive\" }` — done. This should free prefix allocations faster.

oncall-bot: Auto-shedder: prefix caching disabled for large contexts on nyc-gpu-4.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Routing update requested — reroute rule applied for customer chat-qa-prod -> dedicated-2 for 15m.

ryan: pushed routing change (`route apply chat-qa-prod --target dedicated-2 --ttl 900s`). Confirmed 95% of chat-qa traffic now out of nyc-gpu-4.

danielle: after drain + restart + kvcache eviction we see OOM event rate drop from ~12/min to ~0-1/min across the pool. GPU mem use on hosts moved from ~92% -> ~58% on average.

robin: looking at nvml and slab stats: fragmentation was high, likely due to long-lived KV entries + large context allocations. Restart helped coalesce. Good catch.

samir: customer impact summary (initial window 10:02–10:23 UTC):
- chat-qa-prod: intermittent 503s and elevated latency (p95 from 120ms -> 1.9s). estimated affected requests ~3.2k.
- summarizer-labs: occasional failures during 10:10–10:20 UTC (fallback to smaller model).
Support-bot: Notified #support-alerts, opened INC-8742-REDWOOD with details and affected tenants.

samir: mitigation state: traffic rerouted, aggressive eviction enabled, rolling restarts complete, OOM rate normalized. Marking status: mitigated -> monitoring.

danielle: action items / follow-ups:
- add detection rule for rapid long-context allocation bursts (token-window > 2000 spikes).
- add autoscale rule to spin additional dedicated capacity before aggressive OOM threshold.
- add per-customer soft token cap to prevent single tenant from exhausting shared pools.
- postmortem + timeline to be drafted in #postmortems.

ryan: adding temporary guard in routing: prefer fallback-medium for any request > 4096 tokens for next 24h.

samir: pinging SRE lead @robin for postmortem triage and customer comms.

robin: will own postmortem. initial priority: tuning autoscaler and kvcache eviction heuristics. Also recommend a small instrumentation change to report alloc-size histogram.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD-INC-8742 status changed to Resolved by samir (duration ~21m). If anything recurs, please re-open or escalate.

samir: closing thread here — keeping monitoring for 30m. If anyone sees new OOMs please tag me. :thumbsup:
